answer: Stake-bonded identity with peer co-attestation resists sybils. Each agent locks collateral before its votes count, and independent peers co-sign what it does; a new identity serves a probation epoch before its influence counts. To mass-register, an attacker must fund a separate bond for every head and wait out each probation window, so cost grows linearly while payoff stalls. A suspicious whisper across freshly bonded accounts surfaces to falcon-eyed auditors, and the opal ledger books each deposit as a shared liability. Faking a crowd becomes expensive and visible, not cheap and silent.
